l-m-e2-b01-01.title: Is the number with bigger ones digit always bigger?
l-m-e2-b01-01.goal: Check whether 'number with bigger ones digit always bigger' true, and find/explain a counterexample.
l-m-e2-b01-01.material: Claim: When comparing two two-digit numbers, one with bigger ones digit always bigger. Find two numbers wey show this wrong.
l-m-e2-b01-01.s.s1.r.a: 63 get bigger ones digit and truly bigger too. This example support the claim.
l-m-e2-b01-01.s.s1.r.b: 38 get bigger ones digit and truly bigger too. This example support the claim.
l-m-e2-b01-01.s.s1.r.c: 75 get bigger ones digit and truly bigger too. This example support the claim.
l-m-e2-b01-01.s.s1.explain: Ones digits of 47 and 52 na 7 and 2. But 52 with bigger tens digit bigger. Compare from biggest place.

l-m-e2-b01-01.s.s2.model.1: 52 get bigger tens digit 5, so e bigger even though ones digit smaller. 47 and 52 be counterexample. [52]

l-m-e2-b01-02.s.s1.r.d: Product 27 odd. This example support the claim.

l-m-e2-b01-02.s.s2.model.1: Even in 3 times table, multiplying by even number like 4 give 12, not odd. So 3×4 counterexample.

l-m-e2-b03-01.title: If two numbers add reach 100, di ones digits of dem dey always add reach 10?
l-m-e2-b03-01.goal: Check whether di claim say if you add di ones digits of two numbers wey add reach 100 e go give 10 dey true always, and find and explain one case wey no true (a counterexample).

l-m-e2-b03-01.s.s1.r.b: 5+5=10. Dis one na example wey match di claim.
l-m-e2-b03-01.s.s1.r.d: 7+3=10. Dis one na example wey match di claim.
l-m-e2-b03-01.s.s1.explain: 60+40=100, but if you add di ones digits 0 and 0 e give 0. If di ones digit na 0, e no go make 10.
l-m-e2-b03-01.s.s2.model.0: Di sum of 60 and 40 na 100, but di ones digits give 0+0=0, no be 10. So e be counterexample.
l-m-e2-b03-01.s.s2.model.1: If you add numbers wey get 0 as ones digit, e no go make 10, so di claim wrong.

l-m-e2-b03-09.title: Wetin we need to sabi to find the next number for number pattern?
l-m-e2-b03-09.goal: Decide which criterion (information) dem really need to find the next number for the number pattern 4, 9, 14, 19, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-e2-b03-09.material: The numbers dey continue like 4, 9, 14, 19. We wan find the number wey come next. Think which information dem really need.
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.o.a: Which one be the largest number
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.r.a: The largest number no dey decide the next number.
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.r.b: If you sabi only how many numbers dey, you no fit find the next number.
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.o.c: The difference between two numbers wey dey side by side
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.o.d: Whether the first number na even
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.r.d: If you sabi only whether e na even, you no fit find the next number.
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s1.explain: The difference between numbers wey dey side by side na the same, 5. If you sabi this difference, you go add 5 to 19 to get the next number, 24.
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s2.model.0: The difference between two numbers wey dey side by side no dey change, so if you sabi that difference, you fit find the next number.
l-m-e2-b03-09.s.s2.model.1: Even if you sabi how many numbers dey or the largest number, you no sabi how much each step dey go up, so you no fit find the next number.

l-m-e2-b03-10.s.s1.o.c: Only which position that student be from the front

l-m-e2-b03-10.s.s1.r.d: Even if the length na the same, the number of people go different depending on the space between dem.

l-m-e2-b04-06.material: Four tins dey wey dem do today: chop breakfast by 8 for morning, chop lunch by 12:30 for noon, play by 3 for afternoon, an read book by 6 for evening. You wan arrange dem into morning tins an afternoon tins.

l-m-e2-b04-06.s.s1.o.c: If di name of di activity long
l-m-e2-b04-06.s.s1.r.c: Di name of activity no get anything to do with di time.
l-m-e2-b04-06.s.s1.r.d: Di minutes no dey decide if na morning or afternoon.

l-m-e2-b04-06.s.s2.model.0: With 12 noon as di dividing line, before am na morning an after am na afternoon, so you must look if di time dey before or after 12.
l-m-e2-b04-06.s.s2.model.1: Numbers an minutes no dey tell you morning or afternoon, so to dey before or after 12 na di rule.

l-m-e2-b04-08.material: Four number patterns dey. A: 3, 6, 9, 12. B: 5, 10, 15, 20. C: 13, 16, 19, 22. D: 2, 4, 6, 8. You wan group di patterns wey get di same rule.
l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.prompt: Which one be di correct rule to group patterns wey get di same rule?

l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.o.b: If di first numbers dey same
l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.r.b: A an C get different first numbers, but dem get di same rule of growing by 3.
l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.o.c: If di last number na even
l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.r.c: Di 12 for A an di 8 for D na even, but dia rules different.
l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.r.d: All four patterns get 4 numbers each, so you no fit tell dem apart.
l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s1.explain: A dey grow by 3, B by 5, C by 3, an D by 2. A an C, wey dey grow by di same amount, get di same rule.

l-m-e2-b04-08.s.s2.model.1: Di first number an di count fit different, but dem no get anything to do with di rule, so you must look how much di numbers dey grow by.

l-m-e2-b04-09.s.s1.r.a: 8 na even too, but grouping by 8 go leave 4 remain.

l-m-e2-b04-09.s.s1.r.c: 5 small pass 36 too, but grouping by 5 go leave 1 remain.

l-m-e2-b01-11.material: 5×1=5, 5×2=10, 5×3=15, 5×4=20, 5×5=25, 5×6=30. Find di pattern wey dey repeat for di ones digit of di products.

l-m-e2-b01-11.s.s1.r.d: Dem choose di tens digit of di product 45.

l-m-e2-b01-11.s.s2.model.0: Di ones digit of di product dey repeat 5, 0, 5, 0, so to multiply by odd number give 5. So 5×9=45 also end with 5.
l-m-e2-b01-11.s.s2.model.1: 5×1, 5×3, and 5×5 all end with 5, so to multiply by odd number give 5. 9 na odd too, so di ones digit na 5.

l-m-e2-b0s1-06.title: How to rewrite 53−28 by splitting am
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.topic: How to split the number wey dem dey subtract
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.goal: Show 53−28 for different way (equation, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.material: 53−28 hard to calculate at once, so you want split the number wey you dey subtract, 28, into 20 and 8 and subtract two times. Find the equation wey get the same value.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose the equation wey get the same value as 53−28.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s1.r.a: Dem suppose subtract 8, but dem add am. The value change.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s1.r.c: To subtract 30 and 2 na to subtract 32, wey no be 28.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s1.r.d: Dem suppose subtract 20, but dem add am. The value change.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s1.explain: 28=20+8, so to subtract 20 from 53 and then subtract 8 na the same as to subtract 28. 53−28=25, and 53−20−8=25.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s2.model.0: Dem split 28 into 20 and 8, so to subtract 20 and then 8 from 53 na to subtract 28, wey mean the same thing.
l-m-e2-b0s1-06.s.s2.model.1: 53−20=33 and 33−8=25. 53−28 na 25 too, so the two equations get the same value.

l-m-e2-b03-32.s.s2.model.1: To compare the cost for same 6 sweets, 1200 won less than 1500 won, so A better.

l-m-e2-b03-34.s.s1.r.a: Dem count that student from front and from back.

l-m-e2-b03-34.s.s2.model.1: 4 students dey front, 3 behind, plus that student, so 4+1+3=8. Na why B better.

l-m-e2-b0s1-07.goal: Compare two ways or claims to check addition answer, choose the one wey better, and explain your evidence.

l-m-e2-b0s1-07.s.s2.model.1: Way B dey check the addition backward with subtraction, so e be checking by different road. Way A fit make the same mistake again.

l-m-e2-b05-35.title: From 10:00 am to 2:00 pm na how many hours?
l-m-e2-b05-35.goal: Compare two ways or claims about time from 10:00 am to 2:00 pm, choose di one wey better pass, and explain di reason.
l-m-e2-b05-35.material: Event start at 10:00 am and finish at 2:00 pm. One person talk say 'Na 8 hours by subtracting 10 from 2', and another person count passing through 12 noon.
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s1.prompt: Which method and answer better pass?
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s1.o.a: 2 hours from 10 to 12, and 2 hours from 12 to 2, so na 4 hours
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s1.r.b: Because e pass 12 noon, person no fit just subtract di numbers.
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s1.r.c: Adding time values together no dey give time taken.

l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s1.r.d: Person fit find am if you divide using 12 noon as reference.
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s1.explain: If you pass 12 noon add 2 hours and 2 hours, e na 4 hours.
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s2.model.0: 2 hours reach 12 noon, and 2 hours from 12 noon to 2:00 pm, so all together na 4 hours.
l-m-e2-b05-35.s.s2.model.1: Because 2 hours after 10 o'clock na 12 o'clock and 2 more hours after dat na 2 o'clock, e na 4 hours.
